title: DebianBuildReportV1
description:
The full 2A.1 build report.

The 2A.1 stub fills `schema_version`, `report_kind`, `outcome: Pass`, and `producer: { name, version }`; the rest is `Default::default()`. 2A.3 fills every field from real sbuild output.

diagnostics.description: Per-check failure / informational lines. Empty when `outcome` is `Pass`. The normalizer propagates these as `Observation`s on the `NormalizedResult` for the `BuildValidation` gate's evidence row.

exit_code.description: The tool's exit code. The 2A.1 stub always reports `0`; 2A.3 reports the real sbuild exit code.

finished_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of build finish. The 2A.1 stub leaves this empty; 2A.3 fills from the tool's `finished_at` clock.

outcome.description: The tool's classification of the build outcome. The normalizer reads this field and maps it to an `EvidenceStatus` or `NormalizationError`.

producer.description: The producer block (tool name + version + build-environment id).

references.description: References to build artifacts (build log, `.changes`, `.buildinfo`, binary debs).

started_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp of build start. The 2A.1 stub leaves this empty; 2A.3 fills from the tool's `started_at` clock.

ArtifactRef.description: One reference to a build artifact (the build log, the `.changes`, the `.buildinfo`, the generated `.deb`s). The 2A.1 stub leaves `references` empty; 2A.3 populates it with the build log + `.changes` + `.buildinfo` (binary debs come in 2A.x follow-on).

path.description: The on-disk path of the artifact (relative to the build output dir).

BuildOutcome.description:
The tool's classification of the build outcome. The normalizer reads this field and maps it to an `EvidenceStatus` (Pass / Fail) or to a `NormalizationError` (Unclassifiable for the non-defect cases, per the spec's "Unknown failure modes must not be silently classified as package defects" rule).

Note: `Malformed` and `MissingTool` are **normalizer-only** cases, not `BuildOutcome` variants. The tool never emits `outcome: "malformed"` or `outcome: "missing_tool"` in its JSON; the normalizer detects those cases from the `ExecutionRecord`'s `stdout` / `exit_code` fields before parsing the report.

oneOf.description: The build failed for a package-defect reason (compile error, missing build-dep, etc.). Normalizer returns `EvidenceStatus::Fail` with the report's `diagnostics` as observations.

The build failed for an infrastructure reason (sbuild chroot missing, network down, etc.). Normalizer returns `NormalizationError::Unclassifiable(...)`, which the runtime maps to `Outcome::InfrastructureFailed` → `GateStatus::Blocked`.
Catch-all. The tool saw a failure it could not classify. Normalizer returns `NormalizationError::Unclassifiable(...)` — **never `Fail`**, per the spec. The `String` payload is the tool's reason text.

BuildProducer.description: The producer block. The 2A.1 stub sets `name: "ironmaint-debian-tool"` and `version: env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")`; 2A.3 sets `name: "sbuild"` and the real sbuild version.

build_environment_id.description: A stable identifier for the build environment (e.g. a container image SHA-256, or a `sbuild` schroot identifier). The 2A.1 stub leaves this empty.

BuildProvenance.description: The provenance block. The candidate fingerprint, commit, and tree are the candidate's identity; the 2A.1 stub fills these from `BUILD_FINGERPRINT` / `BUILD_COMMIT` / `BUILD_TREE_SHA` env vars (which the runtime will inject in 2A.2; the 2A.1 stub leaves them empty when the env is unset).

BuildSourcePackage.description: The source-package identity block. Populated from `debian/control` `Source:` and `debian/changelog` in 2A.3; the 2A.1 stub leaves them empty.

BuildTargetInfo.description: The build target. Same shape as `BuildTarget` (the 2.0-C adapter-api type). The 2A.1 stub fills from `BUILD_TARGET_SUITE` / `BUILD_TARGET_ARCH` env vars.

Diagnostic.description: A single failure or informational line from the tool.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable error code, e.g. `E_DEBIAN_DIR_MISSING`. Future tools can match on this without parsing the message.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. The tool does not embed the offending value (a) to keep PII out of the report and (b) so the same diagnostic text can serve any fixture.

path.description: The on-disk path that triggered the diagnostic, when applicable (e.g. `debian/`, `debian/changelog`).
